# solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-flash_10-budgetprompt

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Same as the `solo` baseline (100 steps, compaction at 28K), plus one paragraph at the end of the task prompt saying the agent has at most 100 steps and that only pushed and submitted work counts. Tests whether simply knowing the limit makes agents submit in time.

## Observations

- 0/10. All 10 agents were stopped at step 100 with nothing pushed. Even `pallets_jinja_task/1621` committed its work near the end but did not push before the limit.
- No agent mentioned the step limit in its reasoning. The agent sees the limit on every call, but nothing tells it which step it is on, and summarizing the context removes the history it could count from. Showing the current step number on every turn is the next thing to test.
